mcq.s: One of the problems in calculating National Income in India is:
mcq.x: The large unorganised sector (small units, agriculture) keeps no proper accounts, making national income estimation difficult; double counting and the non-monetised sector are other problems.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding stabilisation and structural adjustment as two components of the new economic policy adopted in India?
o: Stabilisation is a gradual, multi-step process, while structural adjustment is a quick adjustment process
Structural adjustment is a gradual, multi-step process, while stabilisation is a quick adjustment process
Stabilisation and structural adjustment are very similar and complementary policies; it is difficult to separate one from the other
Stabilisation mainly deals with policies to be implemented by the Central Government, while structural adjustment is to be set in motion by the State Governments
mcq.x: Stabilisation is short-term demand management (inflation, fiscal deficit, BoP); structural adjustment is a longer, gradual supply-side reform of trade, industry and finance.

mcq.s: 'Base year' in National Income accounting means:
o: The year whose income is used to calculate the nominal national income
The year whose prices are used to calculate the nominal national income
The year whose prices are used to calculate the real national income
The year whose income is used to calculate the real national income
mcq.x: The base year supplies the reference (constant) prices at which real GDP/national income is valued; India's current base year is 2022-23.

mcq.s: In which of the following years was the annual growth rate of Gross National Income and Net National Income negative in India at both current and constant prices?
mcq.x: In the COVID-19 year 2020-21, GNI and NNI contracted at both current and constant prices, followed by a sharp rebound in 2021-22.
